messages:
maya: Heads-up — noticed several DB backups and object-archive files uploaded by backup-collector lost SSE metadata after we migrated them into the lifecycle bucket. Detected by backup-integrity job. :eyes:
raj: Which keys exactly? any sample objects we can check quickly?
maya: bucket=redwood-backups-lifecycle, prefix=db/2026-03-20. `head-object` shows no x-amz-server-side-encryption header for multiple files.
maya: Command I used:
```
aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-backups-lifecycle --key db/2026-03-20/tenant42.dump.gz
```
raj: hmm. Did the lifecycle copy/transition job rewrite objects? I know archive-mover lambda was updated last week.
oliver: Confirming — we deployed archive-mover v2 that re-writes objects into a new bucket and was supposed to preserve SSE-KMS. It looks like we relied on SDK defaults and didn't set `ServerSideEncryption`. Investigating now.
sre-oncall: Impact assessment — are objects lost or just missing the CMK metadata? Any restore failures yet?
maya: Objects are intact/readable, no corruption. But missing CMK metadata means they won't show as SSE-KMS in audits and might violate some customer contracts. Need containment and remediation.
security-bot: Alert created: ENCOPS-2026-031 — Missing server-side-encryption metadata for ~110 objects. Auto-tagged severity=high.
emily: Short-term: can we re-encrypt in-place? S3 requires copy-with-replace-metadata to set server-side encryption. Suggest copy to same key with `--metadata-directive REPLACE` and `--server-side-encryption aws:kms`.
raj: Proposed immediate mitigation:
1) Remove backup-collector write grant (block archive-mover) until fix is deployed.
2) Run re-encrypt copy for affected objects: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-backups-lifecycle/db/2026-03-20/ s3://redwood-backups-lifecycle/db/2026-03-20/ --recursive --metadata-directive REPLACE --server-side-encryption aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id alias/redwood-cmk`
oliver: Hotfix: change SDK PutObject to set `ServerSideEncryption='aws:kms'` and `SSEKMSKeyId` explicitly; add unit test that validates preserved encryption headers during copy. Will have PR up shortly.
maya: Audit query I ran (BigQuery):
```
SELECT * FROM audit_logs
WHERE resource = 'archive-mover'
  AND action = 'PutObject'
  AND json_extract(metadata, '$.x-amz-server-side-encryption') IS NULL
  AND timestamp >= '2026-03-20'
```
sre-oncall: Priority: run restore tests for a sample of tenants (3) from the affected set using compliance checklist. If restores fail escalate.
emily: Also tighten IAM for backup-collector: restrict kms:Encrypt/Decrypt to the CMK ARN and add condition `StringEquals: {"kms:ViaService": "s3.amazonaws.com"}` where possible.
raj: I'll open a short PR to revoke the write role and schedule the canary re-encrypt job. Oncall — can you run the re-encryption script and post logs here? I'll coordinate the cutoff window.
sre-oncall: Starting re-encrypt now for batch 1, will post progress. :lock:
maya: Action items (owners):
- raj: revoke write grant for archive-mover (P0)
- oliver: hotfix SDK + tests, deploy (P1)
- sre-oncall: run re-encrypt for affected objects, run restore tests (P0)
- emily: update IAM/KMS policy + alert for missing SSE header (P1)
- security: document incident, notify customers per compliance playbook (maya)
oliver: ETA for hotfix ~2h, adding deploy-bot note to track.
sre-oncall: Re-encrypt batch 1 finished: `copied 45 objects, 0 errors`. Proceeding with batch 2.
security-bot: ENCOPS-2026-031 updated with remediation steps and hotfix PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/commit/abcd1234 :+1:
maya: Thanks all — keep updates here. If anything escalates ping #incident-ops and I'll join the war room.
raj: Will follow up with a short postmortem draft once we validate re-encrypt and restore tests.
